record.original_question: Call a non-Gamma II_1 factor N pseudocompact if there exists a non-principal ultrafilter U such that N is elementarily equivalent to the tracial matrix ultraproduct M_U = ∏_{n→U} M_n(C). For n ≥ 2, is the free group factor L(F_n) pseudocompact?

evidence.quote: Problem 3 (Pseudocompactness problem). A non Gamma factor N is said to be pseudocompact if there exists an ultrafilter U such that N is elementarily equivalent to MU. Is L(Fn) pseudocompact for n ≥ 2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A tracial von Neumann algebra is a pair $(M,\tau)$ consisting of a von Neumann algebra $M$ together with a faithful normal tracial state $\tau\colon M\to\mathbb{C}$. A II$_1$ factor is an infinite-dimensional tracial von Neumann algebra with trivial center and a (necessarily unique) faithful normal tracial state. A II$_1$ factor $N$ has property Gamma if there is a sequence of unitaries $u_k\in N$ with $\tau(u_k)=0$ such that $\|[u_k,x]\|_2\to 0$ for every $x\in N$; otherwise $N$ is called non-Gamma.

For each $n\ge 1$, let $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ be equipped with its normalized trace $\mathrm{tr}_n$. Given a non-principal ultrafilter $\mathcal{U}$ on $\mathbb{N}$, the tracial matrix ultraproduct is the II$_1$ factor
$$M^{\mathcal{U}} \;=\; \prod_{n\to\mathcal{U}} M_n(\mathbb{C}) \;=\; \ell^\infty(\mathbb{N},(M_n(\mathbb{C}))_n)\big/\{(x_n): \lim_{n\to\mathcal{U}}\mathrm{tr}_n(x_n^*x_n)=0\}.$$

Two tracial von Neumann algebras are elementarily equivalent if they satisfy the same sentences in the continuous first-order language of tracial von Neumann algebras (equivalently, by the Keisler–Shelah theorem in the continuous setting, they have isomorphic ultrapowers).

Call a non-Gamma II$_1$ factor $N$ pseudocompact if there exists a non-principal ultrafilter $\mathcal{U}$ on $\mathbb{N}$ such that $N$ is elementarily equivalent to $M^{\mathcal{U}}$.

For an integer $n\ge 2$, let $\mathbb{F}_n$ denote the free group on $n$ generators and let $L(\mathbb{F}_n)$ be the associated free group II$_1$ factor (the von Neumann algebra generated by the left regular representation of $\mathbb{F}_n$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{F}_n)$). It is known that $L(\mathbb{F}_n)$ is a non-Gamma II$_1$ factor.

Question: For every integer $n\ge 2$, is $L(\mathbb{F}_n)$ pseudocompact?
artifact.category_tag: II_1 factors and continuous model theory
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to still be open. Recent work has produced the first explicit examples of non-Gamma II$_1$ factors that are not elementarily equivalent to any matrix ultraproduct, but whether the free group factors $L(\mathbb{F}_n)$ are elementarily equivalent to a matrix ultraproduct is explicitly stated as unresolved; even the question of whether $L(\mathbb{F}_m)$ and $L(\mathbb{F}_n)$ are elementarily equivalent for $m\ne n$ remains open.

status_evidence.title: An exotic II_1 factor without property Gamma
status_evidence.snippet: ...first explicit example of a II_1 factor without property Gamma that is also not elementarily equivalent to any ultraproduct of matrix algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Constructs non-Gamma II_1 factors not elementarily equivalent to a matrix ultraproduct, while leaving the status of L(F_n) open.

status_evidence.title: A Note on Pseudofinite W*-Probability Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known whether L(F_n) is elementarily equivalent to an ultraproduct of matrix algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Recent note reiterates that pseudocompactness of free group factors is open.
